txt: In 1803, the United States doubled in size. Overnight. It paid about three cents an acre. In 1867, it bought a land more than twice the size of Texas. People called it a folly. And in 1946, it secretly tried to buy the biggest island on Earth. With gold.
Eight hundred and twenty-eight thousand square miles. For fifteen million dollars. About three cents an acre.
Alaska is more than twice the size of Texas.
Newspapers called it Seward's Icebox. Some even called it Walrussia.

The price: twenty-five million dollars, in gold. For about one hundred and thirty-four square miles. That's almost three hundred dollars an acre. Compared to Louisiana, about ten thousand times more expensive.
And the answer from Denmark and Greenland was the same: Greenland is not for sale.
Which deal would you have made? And should America still try to buy Greenland? Tell me in the comments.
